9_risks: The existing mixed worktree may contain overlapping user-owned changes; MIG-001 must stop on ambiguous ownership.
A prose facade can appear simpler while silently duplicating or bypassing deterministic gates.
Live provider behavior and costs can change with model or harness versions; conformance evidence must be versioned and dated.
Package-name availability and registry identity can change before release.
Broad legacy deletion before a real vertical proof can remove working capabilities without user benefit.
A polished README can amplify inaccurate claims if evidence generation is not the source of support tables.
Opt-in telemetry may be too sparse for product decisions; local reports and direct beta interviews remain required.
sections.10_rollout: Release in four states: internal developer preview after facade fixtures; private alpha after a replayable Fix loop; public beta after clean package installs, docs, security review, and provider-specific conformance; GA only after the ADLC-MIG-VAL gate and explicit human publication approval. Roll back by reinstalling the prior signed package and provider manifest; keep legacy entry points throughout the beta compatibility window.
11_validation_plan: Validate this Build Brief, readiness report, and clarity gate before dispatch.
Run deterministic unit, contract, installer, compiler, docs, security, compatibility, and clean-tree tests on every PR.
Run trace-based skill pressure scenarios against fixture harnesses on every PR and credentialed providers on the scheduled/release lane.
Record at least one real interruptible Fix loop before broad migration and real Build/Fix/Review runs before published support graduation.
Install the built wheel into clean Python 3.9 and 3.13 environments and exercise install, doctor, update, rollback, and uninstall.
Run independent completion audit with executor and auditor identity evidence.
Validate README examples, docs links, generated provider support table, package metadata, release artifacts, and clean git status from the release tag.
